channel.title: The Bay View Bulletin
channel.description: Bay View's morning paper: daily news for Milwaukee's Bay View neighborhood.

item.title: Developer Tim Olson's group buys the KK and Bay Street corner for $625,000
item.description: The one-acre site at 300 E. Bay St. and 2020 S. KK has two aging buildings; no plans are public yet.

item.title: Mayor signs the 2027 budget with no vetoes, so the council's changes take effect
item.description: It's the first veto-free city budget since 2014, keeping the council's road, library and pay changes in place.

item.title: City proposes zoning changes to allow more housing; comments are open through Dec. 11
item.description: Cottage courts, more townhouses and smaller lots are in the draft; there's a drop-in session Friday at the Zeidler building.

item.title: MPS climbs to 'meets expectations' on new state report cards
item.description: The district rose from two stars; 67 MPS schools met or beat expectations, while 76 fell short.

item.title: Spotlight: Jasher's Organic Tea House
item.description: A living-room tea house tucked into Joyce Skylight Court, with chai made from scratch and a violin solo this Friday

item.title: After the Burrell Street shooting, city orders the party rental to get licensed
item.description: The short-term rental had no city license; Ald. Dimitrijevic says neighbors can now report suspect rentals online.

item.title: How Milwaukee decides which lead water lines get replaced first
item.description: Water Works scores each property, mostly on neighborhood disadvantage; 55,000 homes still had lead lines.

item.title: New this week: MPS chief says school closures and mergers are likely in 10-year plan
item.description: Final Great Schools advisory meeting of the year wrapped Monday; a draft plan could come in January.

item.title: Spotlight: Melt Chocolates
item.description: An engineer's Craigslist find became a Bay View chocolate shop with five medals from London's Academy of Chocolate

item.title: Teen wounded in early Sunday shooting near Burrell and Smith streets
item.description: An 18-year-old was hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries; police are still looking for a suspect.

item.title: Torzala and Component plan Black Friday beers at the Lincoln Warehouse
item.description: Both breweries in the Lincoln Warehouse have special releases lined up for Nov. 27.

item.title: City-county Holiday Drive opens today, collecting food and essentials
item.description: Drop off food, tote bags, wipes or toiletries at libraries, City Hall and more for a Metcalfe Park pantry.

item.title: Spotlight: Rush-Mor Records
item.description: Milwaukee's oldest record store has been spinning on the corner of KK and Potter since 1971

item.title: Neighbors refill the Clarence Street Cabinet after an empty-shelf plea
item.description: The free food cabinet on E. Clarence St. went from nearly bare to full in a day as winter demand climbs.

item.title: Milwaukee's Vision Zero plan aims to end traffic deaths by 2037
item.description: On the World Day of Remembrance, the city says 41 people have died on its streets so far this year.

item.title: Mr. Wings pop-up wraps up its run at Happy Dough Lucky tonight
item.description: Wings, hot mini donuts, pizza and pinball on KK through Sunday; the kitchen runs late.

item.title: Spotlight: Lion's Tooth
item.description: Zines, comics and small-press books, plus a tiny bar and book clubs: Bay View's punk-spirited bookstore.

item.title: Nationwide ground stop strands travelers at Mitchell Airport
item.description: A four-hour FAA halt on departures Friday scrambled plans at MKE; airlines warn delays may linger this weekend.

item.title: Outpost's Buy a Slice pie fundraiser is today on KK
item.description: Grab a slice of pie for a suggested $5 donation at Outpost, 11 a.m. to 2 p.m.

item.title: At Random's Magic Forest returns, with hut reservations opening Nov. 25
item.description: The Delaware Ave. lounge is turning its patio into a lit-up winter hideaway of heated cocktail huts again.

item.title: Spotlight: Cactus Club
item.description: From a 1950s country bar to the room where the White Stripes played: Bay View's tiny, all-ages music landmark.

item.title: MPS chief: a $58 million deficit and fewer students than expected
item.description: In her first State of Our Schools speech, Cassellius said the district's budget gap has grown as enrollment slipped.

item.title: The gas station owner on Bay View's southern edge who knows customers by name
item.description: WUWM profiles Faisal Bhimani, whose two stations at Howard and Clement double as a neighborhood hub.

item.title: Aerial Hippie brings circus-style fitness to the Hide House
item.description: WISN visited the Bay View studio where beginners learn to climb and spin on hanging fabric.

item.title: MPS rebids the Lincoln Avenue School demolition a third time
item.description: After a bidder objected, the fire-damaged school's demolition will now go to the lowest qualified bid.

item.title: Restored Vietnam Veterans Memorial rededicated on the lakefront
item.description: About 100 Vietnam veterans gathered in Veterans Park for the unveiling of a $1 million restoration.

item.title: Friday fish fry: where to find one in Bay View tonight
item.description: Beer-battered cod on Howell, Dutch-style haddock on KK, Vietnamese swai and a Conway Street classic.

item.title: Cat of the Week: Skeeter wants to go home with a sibling
item.description: A playful orange tabby, born in April, is up for adoption along with his littermates.

item.title: Spotlight: Three Brothers
item.description: Seventy years in an old Schlitz tavern: Bay View's Serbian landmark still makes burek the way Mama did.

item.title: Bread and Jam's free community meal ends its current run with a Thanksgiving feast
item.description: The church's weekly free meal, running since 1994, ends its current form with a Nov. 29 feast.

item.title: Mayor's deadline for budget vetoes is Tuesday, and Bay View's street-light fix is in the mix
item.description: Johnson has until Tuesday to sign or veto a budget with more street-light repair crews.

item.title: We Energies rate hike approved, but smaller than requested
item.description: Bills will go up again, by less than the utility asked; the Common Council wants to study a city takeover.

item.title: Leaf rake-out extended two weeks, to Nov. 29
item.description: Late-falling leaves bought everyone more time: rake or bag them through Sunday, Nov. 29.

item.title: Winter parking rules start Dec. 1: check your block now
item.description: No overnight parking on bus routes like KK from Dec. 1, and snow emergencies mean alternate sides.

item.title: MPS Superintendent gives her State of Our Schools address today
item.description: Cassellius lays out district priorities this morning at Discovery World.

item.title: Last community meeting before MPS drafts its school closures plan
item.description: Monday's 6 p.m. session at North Division is the last before a closures plan.

item.title: Bay View housing snapshot
item.description: Median list price about $350,000; 17 homes sold in the past month.

item.title: Ways to help this month
item.description: Serve at Bread and Jam's last feast, give blood Dec. 3, or catch a veterans benefit show.

item.title: The Miz is the NL Cy Young winner, unanimously
item.description: The Brewers' Jacob Misiorowski won the NL Cy Young in a unanimous vote.

item.title: Spotlight: URSA
item.description: The sunny lifestyle shop across from the library has been a KK fixture since 2017, and this Sunday it's emptying the staff's closets.

item.title: History: The North Chicago Rolling Mill (the iron works Bay View grew up around) as it looked in 18…
item.description: The North Chicago Rolling Mill (the iron works Bay View grew up around) as it looked in 1882. The village of Bay View had incorporated three years earlier with 2,592 people as Milwaukee's first suburb, and residents voted to join the city in 1887.

item.title: History: Bay View governed itself as a village for eight years before its roughly 4,000 residents v…
item.description: Bay View governed itself as a village for eight years before its roughly 4,000 residents voted in 1887 to join Milwaukee, becoming the city's 17th Ward. The trade gave up independence for city services residents wanted, such as sewers, sidewalks and street lights. The Beulah Brinton House, pictured, was an early gathering place for the village and is now home to the Bay View Historical Society.

item.title: History: Groppi's: the 1913 Italian grocery that got a second life
item.description: In November 2003, months after the last Groppi closed it, the 90-year-old Italian grocery at Russell and Wentworth reopened under new owners. It's still there.

item.title: History: The Avalon's comeback: Bay View gets its movie palace back
item.description: In November 2014, after 14 dark years and a $2.5 million restoration, the 1929 Avalon Theater on KK announced its reopening. It's still showing movies today.

item.title: History: St. Augustine's steeple rises over Howell Avenue
item.description: In November 1908, Bay View's German Catholics dedicated St. Augustine of Hippo Church on Howell Avenue, the Brust & Philipp landmark still standing 118 years later.

item.title: History: Kneisler's White House, Bay View's tavern "Capitol"
item.description: In the early 1890s, William Kneisler opened a turreted tavern at KK and Ellen. For a century, Kneisler's White House was where Bay View talked politics.

item.title: History: Puddler's Hall, the iron workers' union hall that became a tavern
item.description: In the early 1870s, Bay View's iron puddlers built a union hall on St. Clair Street. More than 150 years later, Puddler's Hall is still pouring.
